tools.name: search_companies
tools.title: Search Companies
tools.description: Search Norwegian companies — complete, enriched profiles incl. roles, annual reports, shareholdings, and web address when found with the authenticated user's NorData API key. Read-only. Supports full-text search (q), filters, sorting, geosearch on coordinates (radius, bounding box, polygon) and field selection (attributesToRetrieve). For the exact filter, sort and geosearch syntax, call get_search_syntax_guide first. Nearby-location questions are answered with a geosearch filter around the location's coordinates. attributesToRetrieve keeps large result sets focused. Industry and municipality are matched by code: look up industry codes with get_norwegian_industry_codes and municipality numbers with get_norwegian_municipalities, then filter on hovedenhet.meta.prefixes.naeringskode1.kode and hovedenhet.forretningsadresse.kommunenummer. q matches company names and text, so a request such as 'IT konsulent Drammen' (IT consultants located in Drammen) is expressed as an industry and municipality filter.

inputSchema.description: Provide at least one of "q" or "filter". This requirement is validated by the MCP server at runtime.

q.description: Full-text query value mapped to Meilisearch q. q matches company names and text. Industry and municipality constraints belong in filter, using codes from get_norwegian_industry_codes and get_norwegian_municipalities; for example, 'IT konsulent Drammen' means IT consultants located in Drammen and maps to a filter, not a q value.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits to return.

offset.description: Number of hits to skip for pagination.

filter.description: Filter expression mapped to Meilisearch filter. Syntax: provide one string in the form `attribute OPERATOR value`; combine clauses with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses. Supported operators include =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, TO, EXISTS, IS EMPTY, IS NULL, IN, CONTAINS, and STARTS WITH; CONTAINS and STARTS WITH depend on upstream experimental support. Quote string values with whitespace or operator-like tokens, and only reference attributes listed in the endpoint's filterableAttributes. Geo filters are supported on geosearch-capable endpoints with _geoRadius(lat, lng, meters), _geoBoundingBox([northLat, westLng], [southLat, eastLng]), and _geoPolygon([lat,lng], ...). For the complete search parameter guide, call get_search_syntax_guide. For company sector/industry plus place requests, use filter-only constraints such as hovedenhet.meta.prefixes.naeringskode1.kode = '62.2' AND hovedenhet.forretningsadresse.kommunenummer = '3301' for IT consultants in Drammen.

parameterUseCases.title: Look up a company by organization number or a precise name
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user gives an organization number, or when matching the text only against company identity fields is safer than searching every searchable field.

parameterUseCases.title: Find companies connected to a named role person
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user names a person and wants companies where that person appears in registered company roles. Start with full-name role search for tolerant matching, then inspect the returned roles to identify the matching person entries.
notes: The full-name field is useful for tolerant name matching across first name, middle name, and surname.
For common names, the exact person can appear after the first small result page; increase limit, page through results, or use exact name-part filters when the spelling is known.
When exact name parts are known, filter on rollegrupper.roller.person.navn.fornavn, rollegrupper.roller.person.navn.mellomnavn, and/or rollegrupper.roller.person.navn.etternavn to select candidates.

Company records can contain several role entries. After using name-part filters, inspect the returned rollegrupper.roller array and keep the role entries where the same person object matches the intended name.
Retrieve rollegrupper.roller.person.id when the next step is to find all roles for the same person across companies.

parameterUseCases.title: Find companies by primary industry code at any level
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks for companies in a sector, industry, NACE division, or Norwegian naeringskode level. Prefer an industry-code filter over q/name matching for sector or industry requests; call get_norwegian_industry_codes first if the user gives an industry name instead of a code.

parameterUseCases.title: Find companies by industry and municipality
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks for a company category in a named place, for example 'IT consultants in Drammen'. Resolve the industry with get_norwegian_industry_codes and the place with get_norwegian_municipalities, then call search_companies with filter constraints instead of q='IT konsulent Drammen'.

parameterUseCases.title: Find companies connected to a known role-person ID
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this after a previous company-role search returned a rollegrupper.roller.person.id and the user wants every company where that same role person appears.
notes: The person ID is a NorData Search API role-person identifier for linking role records across company hits; it is not a national identity number.
The ID must usually be obtained from an earlier response where rollegrupper.roller.person.id was included in attributesToRetrieve.
Filtering by person ID selects matching company documents. Inspect returned roles to show the matching person's role type, name, and whether the role is marked as resigned.
During index backfill, some role entries can be missing person.id. Prefer entries with an ID for cross-company lookups and ignore missing IDs when choosing the follow-up identifier.

firstStepExample.description: Find the registered CEO role for a known company, then read the returned person.id from the DAGL role entry.

secondStepExample.description: Use the returned person.id to find other companies where the same person has roles.

parameterUseCases.title: Find companies by shareholder name
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user names a shareholder and wants companies where that person or organization appears in the shareholder register.
notes: aksjeeierbok contains shareholder register entries for the company.
Use aksjeeierbok.navnAksjonaer in attributesToSearchOn for shareholder-name q searches.
Shareholder data is still being ingested and is currently expected mainly up to about 2020; prefer 2020 or earlier years in example filters until newer years are available.
Some shareholder rows can be incomplete while ingestion continues; present available identifiers, locations, share classes, and share counts when the shareholder name is missing.
Filtering on aksjeeierbok.* selects candidate company documents. Retrieve the shareholder fields and inspect the returned aksjeeierbok array before presenting exact shareholder rows.
Use aksjeeierbok.antallAksjer and aksjeeierbok.antallAksjerSelskap to compare the holding with the company's registered share count.

parameterUseCases.title: Find shareholders of a specific company
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks who owns a specific company, either by organization number or by an exact company name.
notes: Prefer filtering by hovedenhet.organisasjonsnummer when the organization number is known; it returns the single company document whose aksjeeierbok rows should be inspected.

If the user gives an exact registered company name, first resolve it with an exact hovedenhet.navn filter and retrieve hovedenhet.organisasjonsnummer; use q restricted to hovedenhet.navn only for approximate or partial names.
Shareholder data is still being ingested and is currently expected mainly up to about 2020; an empty or missing aksjeeierbok array is not proof that the company has no shareholders.
Some shareholder rows can be incomplete while ingestion continues; present available identifiers, locations, share classes, and share counts when the shareholder name is missing.
Report the ownership year from aksjeeierbok.aar and order returned shareholder rows locally by aksjeeierbok.antallAksjer when explaining who owns the company.

reference.knownIngestionCoverage: Shareholder rows are expected mainly up to about 2020 while ingestion continues.

parameterUseCases.title: Find nearby records from coordinates
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks for items near a place or coordinate. Prefer _geoRadius plus _geoPoint sorting over searching for an address as text.

parameterUseCases.title: Find recently changed companies and inspect change history
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks what changed, or when fresh company records should be prioritized.

parameterUseCases.title: Find companies with address changes in the last 30 days
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks for companies whose business, postal, or location address fields changed in the last 30 days. Filter on root meta.history fields and retrieve meta.history so the matching changes can be inspected.
notes: The cutoff date is generated as 30 days before the current UTC date when the MCP tool metadata is listed.
Use meta.history.felt to match the changed address sub-field; inspect meta.history.gammelVerdi and meta.history.nyVerdi to see the before/after values.

Search filters select candidate company documents. The returned meta.history array can still contain older or unrelated events, so inspect the returned history entries and keep the entries that match the same dato/felt criteria when explaining the result.
Address history can appear for hovedenhet and underenhet events. Use each history entry's type and organisasjonsnummer to identify which unit changed.

parameterUseCases.title: Find companies with CEO role changes in the last 30 days
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks for companies where the Daglig leder/CEO role changed in the last 30 days. Filter role history with meta.history.type = "rolle", role code DAGL, and the relevant handling values.

parameters.filter: meta.history.dato >= "2026-09-18" AND meta.history.type = "rolle" AND meta.history.rolleKode = "DAGL" AND meta.history.handling IN ["lagtTil", "fjernet", "oppdatert"]

notes: Use meta.history.handling = "lagtTil" when you specifically want newly added CEOs.
Role replacements often produce paired fjernet and lagtTil history entries. Use lagtTil to identify the incoming CEO and fjernet to identify the outgoing CEO.

Search filters select candidate company documents. The returned meta.history array can still contain older or unrelated events, so inspect the returned history entries and keep the entries that match the same dato/type/rolleKode/handling criteria when explaining the result.
Use the role code reference to adapt the same pattern to board members, auditors, accountants, and other registered roles.

parameterUseCases.title: Find the largest companies matching financial or staffing criteria
parameterUseCases.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks for ranked company lists by employees or reported accounting fields.

parameterSyntaxReminders: Provide at least one of q or filter when calling a NorData search tool.
Use q for full-text ranking and attributesToSearchOn to restrict which searchable fields q may match.

Use filter for exact constraints, numeric/date comparisons, boolean checks, existence checks, and geosearch constraints; every filter attribute must be listed in this endpoint's filterable attributes.
Use sort only with this endpoint's sortable attributes, or _geoPoint(latitude,longitude):asc/:desc for distance sorting on geosearch-capable endpoints.
Use comma-separated strings for attributesToRetrieve and attributesToSearchOn in this MCP tool, even though raw Meilisearch documents these parameters as arrays.
Use limit and offset together for paging; this MCP tool caps limit at 100.
For company industry-code level searches, use hovedenhet.meta.prefixes.naeringskode1.kode with equality against the desired level, for example '6', '62', '62.', '62.2', '62.20', or '62.200'.
Use hovedenhet.naeringskode1.kode only for exact full-code matches such as '62.200'; it does not match broad levels such as '62'.

For company municipality/place filters, resolve the place name with get_norwegian_municipalities and filter on hovedenhet.forretningsadresse.kommunenummer; do not put place names in q when they are constraints.
For combined industry and place requests such as 'IT consultants in Drammen', resolve both lookup datasets first and call search_companies with filter-only constraints.
For shareholder searches, use aksjeeierbok.navnAksjonaer with attributesToSearchOn and retrieve aksjeeierbok.* fields to inspect the matching shareholder rows.

For ownership-of-a-specific-company requests, filter by hovedenhet.organisasjonsnummer, retrieve aksjeeierbok.* fields, and mention that shareholder ingestion is currently expected mainly up to about 2020.

recordStructure.summary: For company hits, hovedenhet contains the main company's information, aksjeeierbok contains shareholder register entries, and underenheter contains sub-units/sub-companies that should only be used when the user specifically asks for those.
guidance: Prefer hovedenhet.* for ordinary company facts such as name, organization number, legal form, employees, addresses, contact details, and industry codes.
Use aksjeeierbok.* when the task asks about shareholders, owners, share classes, shareholder location, ownership year, or share counts.
Use root meta.history for company change history.
Use underenheter.* only when the task explicitly asks about sub-companies, sub-units, branches, departments, or Norwegian underenheter.
Do not treat underenheter.navn or underenheter.organisasjonsnummer as the main company's name or organization number.

industryCodeFiltering.summary: For company searches by sector or industry, resolve the relevant Norwegian industry code and filter on hovedenhet.meta.prefixes.naeringskode1.kode. This is preferred over q/name matching because company names often do not describe their registered activity. The prefix attribute contains cumulative values derived from hovedenhet.naeringskode1.kode, so equality filters can match broad or narrow industry levels without wildcards.
industryCodeFiltering.appliesTo: Main-company primary industry code only: hovedenhet.naeringskode1. Use underenheter.* only when the user explicitly asks about sub-units.
guidance: When the user asks for companies in a specific sector or industry, identify the best matching industry code and use a filter; do not rely on q matching company names, descriptions, or address text.

If the user gives an industry in words, such as IT consulting, construction, restaurants, retail, fishing, or healthcare, call get_norwegian_industry_codes to find the correct code level before calling search_companies.

If the user phrase combines an industry and a place, such as 'IT consultants in Drammen', resolve both the industry code and municipality number, then call search_companies with filter-only constraints instead of q='IT konsulent Drammen'.
For level-based industry searches, filter with equality on hovedenhet.meta.prefixes.naeringskode1.kode.
Do not use STARTS WITH, CONTAINS, regex, or wildcard filters for industry-code levels; the prefix array already stores each searchable level as an exact value.

For full exact-code matches, hovedenhet.naeringskode1.kode = '62.200' can be used. Use hovedenhet.naeringskode1.kode only when the user supplied the complete code; use the prefix attribute when accepting variable levels from the user.
Use the exact dotted value format from the code level: examples include '6', '62', '62.', '62.2', '62.20', and '62.200'.
Combine the industry-code prefix filter with other filter clauses such as municipality, legal form, employee count, or konkurs status when the user gives additional constraints.

examples.description: Find all companies whose primary industry code is in division 62, such as IT and software-related companies.

Resolve a sector or industry name before searching. For example, if the user asks for IT consulting companies, first call get_norwegian_industry_codes to find the appropriate code, then filter on that code level.

municipalityFiltering.summary: For company searches limited to a Norwegian municipality, resolve the place name to the official four-digit municipality number and filter on hovedenhet.forretningsadresse.kommunenummer. guidance: When the user gives a municipality name, call get_norwegian_municipalities to find the official municipalityNumber, then filter on hovedenhet.forretningsadresse.kommunenummer.

Do not put municipality names such as Drammen, Oslo, or Bergen in q when they are location constraints.
Combine municipality filters with industry-code filters, legal-form filters, employee-count filters, bankruptcy status, or other exact constraints when the user asks for them.

historyModel.shape: Array of history entries on the root meta object.
historyModel.querySemantics: Filtering on meta.history.* returns candidate company documents that have matching history data. When meta.history is retrieved, the response can include the full history array, so post-filter returned entries before presenting the exact changes.
historyModel.valueSemantics: History values such as gammelVerdi and nyVerdi are serialized as strings; empty strings represent blank or cleared values.

historyEventSchema.id: History change id when provided. Several related history entries can share the same id, for example paired rolle entries for a role replacement.

type.summary: The history entry type. Use this to distinguish main-company changes, sub-unit changes, and role changes.

descriptions.hovedenhet: Change to the main company record.
descriptions.rolle: Change to a registered role such as CEO, board member, auditor, or accountant.

historyEventSchema.dato: The date when the change was made, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD.
historyEventSchema.organisasjonsnummer: The organization number the history entry belongs to. For hovedenhet it is the main company number; for underenhet it is the affected sub-unit number. Role entries may omit this field.
historyEventSchema.felt: The property or field the action was applied to, for example "harRegistrertAntallAnsatte" or "forretningsadresse.postnummer". Present for hovedenhet and underenhet entries; role entries use rolleKode/rolleBeskrivelse instead.

handling.summary: Describes what kind of change happened.
handling.note: Role history currently uses lagtTil, fjernet, and oppdatert. Ordinary company/sub-unit field history commonly uses oppdatert.

historyEventSchema.gammelVerdi: The previous value before the change. Values are serialized as strings; an empty string means the previous value was blank or cleared.
historyEventSchema.nyVerdi: The current value after the change. Values are serialized as strings; an empty string means the new value is blank or cleared.
historyEventSchema.rolleKode: Role code for role-related history events.
historyEventSchema.rolleBeskrivelse: Role description for role-related history events.
historyEventSchema.sistEndret: Timestamp for when role-related information was last changed.
historyEventSchema.fratraadt: Whether the person or unit has resigned/left a role when present.
historyEventSchema.person: Person metadata for role-related history events when present, including id, navn.fornavn, navn.mellomnavn, navn.fulltNavn, navn.etternavn, and erDoed.

freshnessAndHistory.retrievalGuidance: Include meta.history in attributesToRetrieve when change history is needed.
notes: updatedAt metadata can appear on the root record and on nested sub-objects; use the most specific level available for the part of the record being inspected.
history metadata is an event list that can explain what changed, when it changed, and the before/after values for property-level changes.

When filtering by history fields, retrieve meta.history and inspect the returned history entries to identify the exact entries that matched the filter; treat the document filter as candidate selection, not as a trimmed history-entry projection.
For company hits, root meta.history contains the indexed change history, including affected organization numbers, changed fields, before/after values, role metadata, and person metadata when present.

For the exact filter, sort and geosearch syntax, call get_search_syntax_guide first. Nearby-location questions are answered with a geosearch filter around the location's coordinates. attributesToRetrieve keeps large result sets focused.

filter.description: Filter expression mapped to Meilisearch filter. Syntax: provide one string in the form `attribute OPERATOR value`; combine clauses with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses. Geo filters are supported on geosearch-capable endpoints with _geoRadius(lat, lng, meters), _geoBoundingBox([northLat, westLng], [southLat, eastLng]), and _geoPolygon([lat,lng], ...). flags.description: Search Norwegian companies — complete, enriched profiles incl. roles, annual reports, shareholdings, and web address when found with the authenticated user's NorData API key.
